key_insight: Voluntarily introducing feedback delays enables high-probability regret bounds with optimal √S and √K dependencies in tabular and linear adversarial MDPs, respectively.
engineering_relevance: The approach advances computationally efficient policy learning with unknown transitions and bandit feedback, without requiring a simulator or exploratory assumptions.
method: Estimate a policy’s Q-function using future episodes while continuing policy updates.
Use Geometric Resampling with Rejection (GRR) to account for policy changes during the delay.
Threshold visitation probabilities to avoid long delays for rarely visited state–action pairs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical high-probability regret guarantees of Õ(poly(H)√(SAK)) for tabular AMDPs and Õ(poly(d,H)√K) for linear AMDPs; no empirical evaluation is described.
watch_item: Optimality applies to the highlighted state-count and episode-count dependencies; polynomial dependence on horizon and feature dimension may still affect practicality.
paper_title: Introducing Feedback Delays to Non-Delayed Adversarial MDPs: Optimal $\sqrt S$ and $\sqrt K$ Dependencies in Tabular and Linear AMDPs
